object_context: In Seregin's Theorem 3.1 F(a)=1 Type-II branch, determine whether the local compactness used to extract a nontrivial ancient Euler limit can transfer any far-field/no-incoming-energy statement from the Navier-Stokes prelimit. Isolate the exact quantifier-order and recentering/tightness obligation before proposing an Euler rigidity theorem.
problem_signature: local strong/weak convergence on every fixed parabolic cylinder
noncompact spatial translations and profile leakage
structural_coordinates: Seregin extraction supplies convergence only on each fixed Q(a): strong L_{3nu}, weak-* L_{2,infty}, weak gradient L2
the target tail statement quantifies R -> infinity and therefore lives outside any one fixed Q(a)
local convergence k -> infinity at fixed R and uniform tail tightness sup_k Tail_k(R) -> 0 as R -> infinity are distinct quantifier orders
translation is noncompact and can move a bounded coherent packet outside every fixed centered ball while preserving global mass/energy
F(a)=1 local energy/pressure/gradient bounds are scale critical and do not themselves supply positive-power decay at large a
the limiting equation is Euler, so viscous Navier-Stokes backward uniqueness is not inherited
pressure is only locally controlled and any global pressure-tail statement requires a consistent normalization/decomposition
nontriviality is source-bound on a fixed unit-scale spacetime quantity and must not be erased by recentering
equivalent_formulations: Uniform-tail form: seek lim_{R->infinity} sup_k Tail(v^lambda_k,q^lambda_k;R)=0 for a source-defined nonnegative tail functional strong enough to pass to the Euler limit.
Quantifier-order form: identify conditions under which lim_{R->infinity} limsup_{k->infinity} Tail_k(R)=0 may be exchanged with the local k->infinity compactness used by the source.

Recentering form: either prove the concentration center remains o(R) relative to the expanding observation scale or work modulo translations with an explicit center trajectory and show no mass/flux is lost.
Signed-flux form: replace absolute tail tightness by a source-inherited signed/telescoping flux potential whose boundary contribution vanishes along a justified sequence of radii/times.
Gluing form: Seregin local ancient-Euler section -> tail/recentering certificate -> exact Euler Liouville theorem -> contradiction with source nontriviality.

explicit_disanalogies: A translated bump is not an Euler or Navier-Stokes counterexample.
The pending XM005 moving-core calibration is proposal-only and cannot supply theorem authority.
The pending PR72 F=1 cutoff result is retrospective proposal-only and cannot be treated as canonical main evidence.
Uniform absolute tail tightness is sufficient for one handoff but may be stronger than necessary; signed telescoping or recentered compactness remain alternative bridges.
Local pressure convergence does not automatically define a global pressure tail because pressure normalization and nonlocal harmonic pieces must be fixed.
Excluding this Type-II source scenario would not solve all Type-II blowup scenarios or the Clay root.
